title.narrative: The Young Women for Awareness, Agency, Advocacy and Accountability (YW4A) Programme

description.narrative: Strengthening the advocacy capacity of 27 women’s rights organizations (WROs) to amplify young women’s voices in Palestine, Egypt, Kenya, and South Sudan by 2025.2.Enhancing the leadership of 17,540 young women to effectively engage in collective action and decision-making in public, private, and civic spaces in Palestine, Egypt, Kenya, and South Sudan by 2025.3.Transforming social norms and practices of 22 faith-based organizations (FBOs) that constrain young women’s rights in Palestine, Egypt, Kenya, and South Sudan by 2025. 4.Influence the adoption, amendment, withdrawal or effective utilisation and implementation of 18 laws and policies towards promoting young women’s rights to leadership, participation and ending SGBV in Palestine, Egypt, Kenya and South Sudan by 2025.

The programme aims to strengthen and diversify young women’s participation and amplify their voices to effectively influence decision-making towards gender-just laws, policies, norms, and practices related to their bodily integrity and equal participation.

title.narrative: WRGE indicator 5.2.2 (WRG049y) : IO2 Strengthened individual leadership of 13,700 young women across the four countries

description.narrative: This indicator refers to the number of young women who are trained TOT and who experience changes in leadership skills, experiences and practices.

title.narrative: WRGE indicator 5.2.2 (WRG049y)# of young women who have gained awareness of their rights, deepened their understanding of women's rights issues, and the ability to generate support around a common cause.competencies towards private and public leadership and advocacy along peers

description.narrative: Under Pathway 2, the YW4A programme enhances the leadership skills of young women through training and creating opportunities for them to train others and exercise their leadership, and be involved in advocacy. Throughout 2022, 700 young women were trained on the RiseUp! Leadership curriculum. Some of these young women have also participated in other trainings, for instance on legal and digital advocacy. The YW4A programme partners participated in various advocacy and dialogue spaces during the year, ensuring the involvement and active participation of young women and WROs.In Kenya the number of young women targeted for training in 2022 was reached. However, due to budget limitations, there was a change in the planned strategy for the year. Instead of engaging the planned 20 young women leads to conduct the training, each of the 350 young women in Cohort 1 recruited two ToTs each, bringing this to 700 young women in Cohort 2 ToTs. Note that the number of young women from Cohort 1 decreased from 356 to 350, because 6 young women had dropped out of the programme in 2022. The 700 young women in Cohort 2 were trained through the FEMspaces methodology, and have gained more because the strategy was developed based on standard operating guidelines which uses a holistic approach of engaging with legal and policy framework, local administrations on domestic violence, psychosocial support where need be and advocacy campaigns. The young women in Cohort 2 are more aware of the referral pathways within their communities.

comment.narrative: Before the RiseUp! Training of Trainers started, 356 Cohort 1 young women took part in the Young Women Leadership (YWL) assessment as to measure their leadership capacity. The YWL score presents the young women's current capacity following the three classifications: Experienced, Aspiring, and Starting. In Kenya the majority of YW were classified as "Experienced" leaders. A smaller but still considerable proportion were in the "Aspiring" stage, demonstrating potential and some leadership experience. Only few of the young women in Kenya were in the "Starting" phase. These trends were consistent among both the general sample and marginalised young women.
The Cohort 1 training target for 2021 was set at 350 young women.

Capacity building activities with young women in Y1 concerned: AK 2.1.1.2 Local adaptation of the YWCA Rise Up! training format and content development, Training of baseline data collectors, Capacity assessment of young women in Cohort 1, AK 2.1.1.1 Data collection workshops, Participatory data analysis workshop, AK2.1.1.3/ AK 2.2.1.4, AK 2.2.1.2 Training of cohort one using RiseUp! Leadership model, life skills training, consultations and identification of advocacy priorities using World YWCA Feminist Consultation Methodology, AK 2.1.1.4 Safe spaces and empowering dialogues same as AK1.4.1.2 Safe and dialogue spaces for the identification of national advocacy priorities.

The total endline target for Kenya was lowered following the MTR, and is now set at 4,300 young women. During 2023 Kenyan partners have trained substantially more young women than anticipated. To achieve the endline target in Kenya, at least 286 young women should be trained in RiseUp! during 2024.

In 2024 one of the YW4A partners continued with the Rise Up! Leadership programme, training a final cohort of young women. The training topics were contextualized to align with national relevant issues, and the young women were actively engaged in safe spaces established by the YW4A partners. A total of 392 young women were trained in 2024, resulting in a total of 4,406 young women being reached, exceeding the country’s set endline target of 4,300 young women. In Kenya, the World YWCA conducted Psychological First Aid (PFA) training, equipping selected Trainer of Trainers with the skills needed to provide essential emotional and psychological support to survivors of GBV and establish referral pathways to governmental and non-governmental agencies. Through this training, young women were empowered as key change agents in their communities and they gained a deep understanding of their role in assisting fellow young women. Additionally, the training emphasized the importance of self-care and emotional well-being.Apart from Rise Up! and other training opportunities, the consortium prioritized initiatives to build young women's leadership skills and confidence through mentorship and platforms to engage with high-level decision-makers. For instance, young leaders were actively involved in various high-level forums, not just as participants but also as panelists and moderators.In 2024, they played key roles in platforms such as Beijing +30, the Human Rights Council 56th session (HRC), and the Sexual Violence Research Initiative (SVRI), showcasing their leadership and advocacy on global stages.
Cohort 1 and 2 will cascade and train another cohort of 1400 young women (cohort 3).

In Kenya, a total of 2,959 young women were reached through the RiseUp! leadership training programme in 2023. This is more than double the initial target. This notable progress was facilitated by the implementation of a school-based approach, which allowed for a significant outreach within schools as a controlled environment. Notably, each school FEM space accommodated approximately 70 girls and over per FEM space. Kenya focused on engaging young women in schools who fall within the age group of 15 to 18 years. This age group was not yet as well represented among the young women participants. The aim was to ensure inclusivity and representation across all age groups, particularly targeting young women in schools to actively involve them in the programme and empower them in their leadership journey.This comprehensive initiative included additional training sessions on social media and legal advocacy facilitated by one of YW4A's technical partners. These sessions aimed to enhance the participants' skills in leveraging social media platforms effectively. The leadership training programme also encompassed sessions on Feminist Consultation Methodology (FCM). This unique approach empowered the young women to advocate for their own issues, drawing from their firsthand experiences and expressing their desires for positive change within their communities. As a result, various young women's groups emerged, initiating their own campaigns to hold leaders accountable for change. Moreover, the training empowered these young women economically, encouraging them to embark on various economic initiatives to support themselves and each other.
The total endline target of 4,300 young women being trained in Rise Up! has been achieved, therefore no targets are set for 2025.

In the final year of YW4A no new young women were trained in the RiseUp! Leadership, as Kenya has achieved its target in 2024. Nonetheless, YW4A continued engaging the trained young women throughout 2025 and the young women actively applied their gained advocacy and leadership skills, and Feminist Consultation Methodology (FCM) to challenge gender norms, particularly through positive masculinity sessions. Monthly check-ins with WROs and lead ToTs facilitated discussions on challenges, leadership development, and strategies to address gender discrimination within school FEMspaces. FEMspaces continued to serve as platforms for economic empowerment, leadership development, and (media) advocacy and advocacy within the young women's communities, for example on the rise in GBV in Kisii County. Despite the existence of legal and policy frameworks, access to GBV services remained low due to stigma, fear of retaliation, and limited public awareness. To address these barriers, weekly radio talk shows were aired on Kisii FM and Radio Vuna, led by young women. The initiative aimed to sensitize the public, amplify survivor voices, promote available support services, and engage duty bearers and community leaders in GBV prevention and response. Also, some of the young women were participants in the Kisii County Finance bill exercise and participated in the public participation exercise and the county programme-based budget analysis. Additionally, a group of YW4A young women drafted and submitted a memorandum to the GBV Technical Working Group Chair, highlighting critical gaps in the local GBV response. The memo outlined several key concerns, including: the absence of government-supported safe spaces for GBV survivors, delayed access to justice for survivors, lack of disaggregated data on femicide, reliance on informal justice systems ("kangaroo courts") that often deny survivors proper legal redress and limited representation of young women in decision-making spaces and leadership structures.
In 2022, the target was calculated based on that each of the 350 young women targeted in 2021 will cascade the training to two other young women, hence the target for 2022 was 700.

title.narrative: WRGE 5.2.1 (WRG045, WRG047, WRG048): IO1 Enhanced capacity of 16-28 WROs to amplify young women's voices

description.narrative: Under IO1 YW4A focuses on enhancing the organisational and advocacy capacity of a selected group of women's rights organisations. The programme also envisages amplifying young women’s voices by promoting that WROs provide space in their internal organisations for young women and establish internal inclusive processes and practices in decision-making, management, and programming. And by working with WROs to include, represent, hear, mentor, support, and prepare young women to take part in advocacy initiatives, link them to strategic decision-making forums, and scale-up local advocacy strategies.

title.narrative: WRGE indicator 5.2.1 (WRG045): # of WROs with enhanced capacity to advance young women’s rights to bodily integrity and equal participation in decision-making.

description.narrative: Under IO1 YW4A focuses on enhancing the organisational and advocacy capacity of a selected group of women's rights organsations through providing training.

comment.narrative: In Kenya YW4A targets a total of 9 WROs under IO1 (organisations with different types of leadership). In Y1 the advocacy and organisational capacity (AOCA) of the participating WROs was measured, as to set the baseline situation. In Kenya the WROs baseline AOCA capacity level is assessed as follows: 1 WRO at GOOD capacity (WRG048); 2 WROs at MODERATE capacity (WRG048, WRG045); 3 WROs at BASIC capacity (1 WRG045; 2 WRG048); 2 WROs at LIMITED capacity (both WRG047). One of the WROs was not yet active at the time of AOCA assessment, hence this organization's baseline will be measured at a later stage.
One of the WROs was not yet active in 2021.

Capacity building activities with WROs in Y1 concerned: AK 1.1.1.2 AOCA Webinar, AK 1.1.1.2 AOCA WRO Inception Meeting, AK 1.1.1 2 AOCA results workshops, AK 1.1.1.2 AOCA collective WRO workshop, AK 1.4.1.2 Safe and dialogue spaces for the identification of national advocacy priorities (1.4.1.2) ; AK 1.1.1.1 Country inception meeting; AK 1.1.1.1 County Inception Meetings.
YW4A continues to work with the same WROs, including the WROs that replaced dropouts.

Capacity building continued throughout 2023, not only through trainings, but also through coalition building and joint advocacy efforts. The results from the AOCA mid-term assessment indicate progress among all seven WROs that were involved in YW4A since the start. A total of six WROs moved up one level on the AOCA scale, and while one WRO enhanced its AOCA measure compared to baseline, it still fell within the same capacity category. Hence in Kenya, 86% of the WROs that joined YW4A since 2021 have met YW4A’s IO1 target to move up one level on the AOCA scale. At mid-term the AOCA capacity of the 9 involved WROs is: 3 WROs at BASIC capacity, 4 WROs with FAIR capacity, 1 WRO at MODERATE and 1 WRO at GOOD capacity.The highest capacity increase is visible in the domain commitment to young women’s voices, while for some organisations applying an intersectional lens to diversify the group of young women reached by YW4A was still a challenge. As a result of the legal & media advocacy trainings the WROs showed a steady increase in their strategic advocacy skills.
During 2025, YW4A continues to target the same WROs (those that take part since the start and new WROs that replaced initial selected WROs).

In its final year of implementation, the YW4A continued to work with the 9 partners in Kenya (6 WROs and 3 FBOs). YW4A continued to build the capacity of the nine organizations in Kenya, for example through (refresher) digital and legal advocacy trainings, equipping young women and organizations with skills to engage policymakers effectively, and contributing to increased participation in legal and policy reforms. There was also strong emphasize on networking and coalition building, among other through participation in different national coalitions such as county level CSO networks, and regional coalitions, to advocate for young women's rights, policy and legal changes jointly with other organizations.The final year also focused on the different endline studies, including conducting the Advocacy and Organizational Capacity Assessment (AOCA). At endline, the AOCA-reassessment and reflection workshop was conducted with the 9 Kenyan organizations, to capture potential changes in their capacity and quantitative AOCA measures compared to baseline and mid-term. Out of the nine organizations in Kenya, all (100%) have moved up at least one capacity level on the 7-point AOCA scale, meaning that in Kenya the YW4A has met the outcome 1 indicator target. Four organizations moved up one level, three organizations moved up two levels, and two organizations – one WRO and one FBO – even moved up three levels.
YW4A continues to work with the same WROs, including the WRO that replaced an organization opting out in 2023.

There were no changes in the composition of the WROs in Kenya during 2024. YW4A continued to build the capacity of the nine organizations. For example through (refresher) digital and legal advocacy trainings, equipping young women and WROs with skills to engage policymakers effectively, and contributing to increased participation in legal and policy reform. There was also strong emphasize on networking and coalition building, among other through participation in different regional coalitions, including the SOAWR Coalition, to advocate for young women’s rights, policy and legal changes jointly with other organizations.
In 2022, YW4A is targeting the same 9 WROs as in 2021. The WRO that was not active throughout 2021, has signed a memorandum of understanding with the partner and became more actively involved.

Throughout 2022, YW4A partners undertook activities to build all WROs’ advocacy and organisational capacity. In Kenya, the nine organisations targeted by YW4A (similar to Y1) took part in these activities. For example, through training on legal and digital advocacy the targeted WROs in Kenya have increased their capacity. Building on legal capacity strengthening undertaken in the first year, partners have enhanced capacity to scale up the critical work they have been doing in addressing women’s rights issues and using their experiences to call for action from duty bearers through various advocacy initiatives in line with the YW4A advocacy priorities and the laws and policies targeted under IO4. They now have the required skills to supplement their legal advocacy campaigns with media strategies. This increased capacity to engage in legal advocacy can also be seen in the way WROs and young women are being strategic when engaging national processes and different policy makers and actors in their country. In Kenya, the nine organisations targeted by YW4A (similar to Y1) took part in these activities.
